title: Read the Labels, Measure the Ticks: A Frontier-Independent Labelling Margin for Training-Free Instrument Reading with a Black-Box VLM

sub_topic: Perceptual blind spots of frontier vision-language models
Analog instrument, scale and clock reading (visual measurement reading)
Training-free tool augmentation and selective prediction for black-box VLMs
primary_focus: Moving the fine-grained measurement out of the frontier model's encoder-to-language readout and into locally measured tick and pointer geometry
A jointly ranked set of scale labellings whose margin is a reliability signal that never passes through the frontier's own visual reading

Committed, pilot-gated accuracy and cost changes on MeasureBench real dials, two further public real-dial sets with frozen thresholds, MeasureBench linear scales and TickTockVQA, under a measured API budget

one_sentence_thesis: Let the frontier model read what an instrument's numbers mean, measure every tick and pointer locally, and trust the reading only when one scale labelling clearly wins.

core_problem.problem_statement: Frontier VLMs read the unit and the rough scale of an analog instrument correctly but get the value wrong: the best reported model is right on 31.5% of MeasureBench real dials and 21.9% of real linear scales while reading the unit 96.2% of the time, and extra thinking barely helps [2510.26865]. The needed signal, the exact position of a thin pointer or meniscus relative to a periodic tick lattice, is lost in the model's visual readout, while trained readers that measure it break on unseen designs [2510.26865][2404.08785][2511.21982].
why_it_matters: Reading gauges, scales and clocks is a basic industrial-inspection and assistive task, and 2026 frontier models still fail it on real gauges while reading in-band digits almost perfectly [2604.22829]; on real industrial scenes the best of 24 MLLMs reaches 25.7% joint value-unit accuracy [2609.04014].

The failure is a readout failure, not a knowledge failure: models identify the instrument, unit and major spacing but miss ticks or whole intervals, answer '10:10' on 11.9-29.7% of real clocks, and do not improve with reasoning [2510.26865]; Astra-style higher reasoning effort costs up to 13.22x and does not close fine-geometry gaps [2609.35718].

Black-box remedies studied so far still end with the frontier model reading pixels (prompts, visual prompts, hints, demonstrations) [2407.06581][2603.16250][2605.16410][2610.12942], and tool-trust arbiters use the same blind model as the judge [2610.04836][2512.06373]; token confidence of a VLM gauge reader yields errors at confidence >= 0.99 [2608.17723].

A 2026 gauge study recommends exactly the split of VLM for semantics and deterministic geometry for the needle, but only as design guidance from three instruments on video [2604.22829]; no one has built it on broad real-image benchmarks, measured when it fails, or given it a reliability signal.

Trained readers modify weights and stay near or below the frontier on real dials (TriSCA 28.5% vs 31.5%) [2604.26614], DialBench's reader 'struggles to predict well on meter images it has never seen before' [2511.21982], and synthetic-data training transfers weakly to real images [2510.26865][2603.08011].
core_problem.concrete_example: A photo of an ammeter whose pointer sits on 20 A: GPT-5 answers 26 A with the correct unit [2510.26865]. The Reitsma modular reader, which anchors the scale on OCR'd numerals, fails OCR on 40-57.5% of images [2404.08785] and scores 8.5% on MeasureBench real images [2510.26865]. On a real wall clock showing 4:37 a frontier model answers '10:10', the output GPT-5 gives on 20.34% of real clocks [2510.26865], and a Sobel+Hough clock reader returns unlabelled lines that score under 10% on in-the-wild clocks [2111.09162]. The proposed system reads the 20 A case as: frontier says box 'C' = 20 and unit A; local geometry puts the pointer 0.02 minor divisions past the major tick labelled by box 'C'; the next-best labelling (box 'C' attached one major over) scores far lower, so it answers 20 A.

key_novelty.main_idea: A frontier-independent labelling margin over locally measured scale geometry
explanation: The frontier model only names things (numeral values in lettered boxes, unit, scale type, pointer roles); every position, tick count and pointer angle is measured locally from the photo.

All nearby ways of numbering the measured ticks (numeral one tick over, a missed tick, swapped hands, reversed direction) are scored together; the gap between the winner and the best answer-changing rival decides whether to answer.
The same labelling-and-margin machinery is run on circular dials, clocks and straight linear scales, and is tested with frozen thresholds on datasets it never saw.

problem_definition.formal_setting: Given an image I of an analog instrument and a question q, recover the reading y (value and unit). After rectification, a circular dial is parameterised by a pivot c and an angle coordinate, and a linear scale by a fitted scale axis and an arc-length coordinate; in both cases the scale is a 1D coordinate u. Locally measured evidence is: tick positions T = {t_1 < ... < t_N} with lengths l_i, numeral boxes B = {(b_j, u_j)} with positions u_j, and indicator positions phi_1..phi_K (pointers, liquid level, object endpoints). The frontier model F, a black box, returns per-box values v_j or 'not a scale numeral', the unit, the scale type s (linear, non-linear, multiple scales) and indicator semantics, but no positions. A labelling hypothesis h = (pi, delta, d, rho) assigns numeral boxes to major-tick indices (pi), inserts or deletes at most one minor tick per major interval (delta), fixes the scale direction (d) and assigns indicator roles (rho: hour/minute/second, decade order, or object start/end). V_h maps a coordinate to a value by local interpolation between flanking labelled ticks. We seek h* = argmax_h S(h; T, B, v, phi) and the margin m = S(h*) - max{S(h): |V_h(phi) - V_h*(phi)| > tol}, where tol is half the measured minor-tick value, computed without ground truth. Output y = V_h*(phi) if m >= tau_m and the pointer-fit quality q >= tau_q, otherwise abstain and fall back to F's own reading y_F.
problem_definition.inputs: One RGB image of an analog instrument (single-pointer gauge, multi-hand clock, multi-dial meter, or single-scale linear instrument) and a natural-language reading question; one API call to GPT-6 Astra at default effort per image; frozen local models on one 24 GB GPU.
problem_definition.outputs: The reading in the instrument's unit (or h:mm for clocks), the labelling margin m, the pointer-fit quality q, an abstain flag, and the intermediate evidence (labelled tick lattice, numeral-to-tick assignment, indicator position) that can optionally be handed back to the frontier model.

key_terms.labelling hypothesis: One complete guess of how the measured ticks are numbered: which major tick each numeral belongs to, whether a minor tick was missed or spurious, the scale direction, and which pointer or endpoint has which role.
key_terms.labelling margin: How much better the best labelling explains the evidence than the best rival labelling that would change the answer by more than half a minor division; a small margin triggers abstention.
key_terms.frontier-independent: Computed only from local measurements and the frontier's symbolic answers (numeral values, unit), never from the frontier's own reading, confidence or self-agreement.
key_terms.tip refinement: A native-resolution, pixel-space fit of the pointer axis from cross-section centroids on concentric circles, seeded by a coarse pointer angle; its precision does not depend on any feature-map patch size.
key_terms.paste-and-compare sweep: Compositing a needle silhouette onto the photo at candidate angles and scoring how little the image changes; used only to pick the coarse pointer angle, tip versus tail, and needle versus shadow.
key_terms.better-views baseline: GPT-6 Astra given the same rectified crop, unwrapped strip and lettered tick and numeral marks that the method computes, but not the computed answer.
key_terms.Astra-best: The single Astra configuration (effort level, tools, views) with the highest pilot accuracy, chosen on the pilot and then fixed for every test set, so the baseline is not a max over noisy test runs.
key_terms.gain decomposition: Gain over a baseline B = coverage x (method accuracy on answered items - B's accuracy on the same items) + (1 - coverage) x (fallback accuracy - B's accuracy on abstained items).
key_terms.coverage: The fraction of images on which the method answers instead of abstaining.
key_terms.frozen thresholds: All score weights and thresholds set once on 200 MeasureBench pilot dials, committed with the code hash and image lists on 2026-10-28, and applied unchanged to every other set.

related_work.sub_area: Frontier VLM evaluation on measurement reading and hard vision
related_work.what_it_does: MeasureBench scores 18 VLMs on 1,272 real instrument images (711 dial, 361 linear, 96 digital, 104 composite) by per-image value intervals; the best model reaches 31.5% on real dials and 21.9% on real linear scales with 96.2% unit accuracy, thinking barely helps, clocks and multi-needle dials are hardest, and real clocks trigger a '10:10' prior [2510.26865]. 'Lost in Motion' evaluates 2026 frontier models on videos of three instruments, finds they fail gauges but read digits near-perfectly, and recommends hybrid architectures with VLMs for 'higher-level semantic tasks' and deterministic edge/Hough pipelines for the needle, plus rule-based validation [2604.22829]. InSituMeasure scores 24 MLLMs on 2,922 real industrial tasks with answerability labels, best 25.7% [2609.04014]. The GPT-6 Astra evaluation shows higher effort and built-in tools close some gaps at 1.04-13.22x cost while metric and fine-structure gaps remain [2609.35718].
related_work.open_gap: These are diagnoses or design guidance. The semantics/geometry split is credited to [2604.22829]; what none provides is a built, single-image system evaluated on broad real-image benchmarks, a reliability signal for when the split fails, or a test of whether the gain comes from measurement or from a better view. Astra has not been measured on dials.

related_work.what_it_does: TriSCA aligns a 4B VLM's visual tower on 400K synthetic triplets, then applies SFT and real-image GRPO, reaching 28.5% on MeasureBench real dials [2604.26614]. DialBench's MRLM injects CLIP template features via cross-attention and MoE, trained end to end on RPM-10K [2511.21982]. A QLoRA-specialised Qwen2.5-VL-7B gauge reader transfers poorly across datasets and its token confidence still gives confident errors [2608.17723]. It's About Time detects the clock, warps it with a learned homography and classifies 720 joint (hour, minute) states, trained on synthetic clocks and pseudo-labelled video, reaching about 80% (minute within +-1) on COCO/OpenImages clocks [2111.09162] but 18.54% full-time on TickTockVQA [2603.08011]. Swap-DPO fine-tunes VLMs with hour/minute-swapped negatives built from theta_h = 30h + m/2 [2603.08011]. A synthetic-only CNN regresses gauge angles with 2-5 degree error on real gauges [2308.14583].
related_work.open_gap: All modify weights, so none helps an API-only frontier model, and their generalisation to unseen designs is weak [2511.21982][2608.17723][2603.08011]. The 720-state joint clock space is learned in [2111.09162]; the hand coupling is used only for training negatives in [2603.08011], never as an inference-time constraint inside a scored hypothesis space.

related_work.what_it_does: Reitsma et al. detect the gauge, find major notches with a trained keypoint head, fit an ellipse, OCR numerals, fit a RANSAC linear angle-to-value map through numeral angles and intersect a segmented needle line; error is 0.77-1.15% of range when OCR reads two or more numerals, but OCR fails on 40-57.5% of images [2404.08785]. MeterFL segments ticks and pointer with a trained 30.6M U-Net, unwraps them into a polar strip and decodes p = i + (theta_ptr - theta_i)/(theta_{i+1} - theta_i) counted from the scale start, with v_min and delta_v supplied, reaching 87.2% within two minor divisions on its public 269-image reading test set, where a zero-shot frontier VLM reaches 49.1% [2609.31998]. A Sobel+Hough clock reader scores 7.7-9.7% on in-the-wild clocks [2111.09162].
related_work.open_gap: Reitsma interpolates linearly between numerals, assumes linear scales and breaks at OCR and needle segmentation; MeterFL needs metadata it does not read and counts from the start, so one missed tick shifts every later index. Neither ranks alternative labellings or abstains, and training-free edge geometry has collapsed in the wild, which is the risk this paper must pass with a day-1-3 pilot.

related_work.sub_area: Render-and-compare and promptable segmentation as training-free pointer localisers
related_work.what_it_does: FoundPose estimates unseen-object pose without training by matching frozen DINOv2 ViT-L layer-18 patch descriptors between a real crop and renders of an exact 3D model; because 14 px patches limit precision it adds featuremetric refinement [2311.18809]. SAM 2 segments any object from a single click on an image, predicting several masks for ambiguous clicks, at 58.9-61.9 1-click mIoU on 23 zero-shot datasets [2408.00714].
related_work.open_gap: Neither has been used to localise a 2-4 px instrument pointer. At patch scale a thin needle is sub-patch, so precision must come from a separately defined pixel-space refinement; the paper therefore compares the frozen-feature sweep against a hub-prompted SAM 2 mask, a radial profile and a pixel-space sweep, all with the same refinement.

related_work.sub_area: Black-box remedies for VLM perceptual blind spots, visual prompting and tool-trust arbitration
related_work.what_it_does: Prompting, CoT and slow thinking do not fix low-level perception although frozen-encoder probes recover it [2407.06581]; Set-of-Mark overlays alphanumeric marks on segmented regions so GPT-4V can refer to them, and warns that numeric marks confuse the model on number-rich images [2310.11441]; task-wise visual prompts [2603.16250], learned hints [2605.16410] and visual demonstrations [2610.12942] steer the black-box model but leave it reading pixels. Tool-trust arbiters use the same backbone VLM to verify specialist outputs [2610.04836] or a trained rethink turn bounded by the model's own grounding [2512.06373].
related_work.open_gap: No black-box method hands the frontier an answer-bearing measurement with a reliability signal that does not pass through the frontier's own visual readout, and none tests whether giving the frontier the same measured views as a visual prompt would close the gap by itself.

related_work.what_it_does: DBNet is a segmentation-based detector for multi-oriented and curved scene text, ResNet-18 variant at 48-62 FPS, trained on generic scene text [1911.08947]. Grounding DINO detects text-named categories zero-shot (52.5 AP on COCO without COCO data) but can hallucinate false positives [2303.05499].
related_work.open_gap: Used here as frozen, benchmark-agnostic components: DBNet localises numerals (the frontier only reads their values), Grounding DINO crops instruments and, on linear scales, the measured object named by the frontier; neither is trained on instrument data.

high_level_flow: Localise: Grounding DINO instrument crop -> ellipse rectification and pivot (dials) or RANSAC scale-axis fit (linear) -> DBNet numeral boxes
Ask once: lettered-box overlay -> single frontier call (box values, unit, scale type, indicator semantics, own reading y_F; minors-per-major only as a soft prior)
Measure: unwrap to a 1D scale strip (polar for dials, axis-aligned for linear) -> tick lattice with local major/minor split and locally counted minors per major
Label: enumerate neighbouring labelling hypotheses -> joint scoring -> winner h* and margin m

Locate indicator: coarse candidate (paste-and-compare sweep on dials and clocks; profile change-point or SAM 2 object mask on linear scales) -> native-resolution tip refinement -> clock-hand or decade coupling check
Answer: local interpolation between flanking labelled ticks -> answer or abstain (fallback to y_F) -> optional evidence hand-back

modules.role: Crop each instrument and map dials to a fronto-parallel circle with a pivot, or linear scales to a straight axis.
modules.model: Grounding DINO-T (Swin-T) frozen, prompt 'gauge dial . clock face . meter dial . ruler . measuring cylinder . thermometer' [2303.05499]; RANSAC ellipse fit on radial edge points (dials); RANSAC line fit on short parallel edge segments (linear scales)
outputs: one rectified crop per instrument at the source's native resolution (no downsampling)
pivot c and rim radius R (dials) or scale axis and tick side (linear)
modules.notes: The detector is used only when the instrument covers less than about half the image or several instruments are present. Grounding DINO's false positives [2303.05499] are filtered by requiring periodic tick-like structure along the fitted ellipse or axis. The pivot is refined as the point minimising the spread of line-segment directions through the hub region.

modules.role: Find where the scale numerals are, without reading them.
modules.model: DBNet ResNet-18, off-the-shelf scene-text weights, frozen [1911.08947]
outputs: numeral boxes b_j with scale coordinate u_j (angle about the pivot, or position along the axis)
modules.notes: Positions come from the local detector, never from the frontier. Boxes off the dominant numeral radius or axis offset are kept but flagged so that the frontier can label them 'not a scale numeral'. Detection recall is a reported component metric on the 150 annotated held-out dials.

modules.role: Read what the frontier is good at: numeral values, unit, scale type, indicator roles, rotation directions on multi-dial meters, and its own reading as fallback.
modules.model: GPT-6 Astra through its API, default reasoning effort, exactly one call per image
inputs: rectified crop with each DBNet box outlined and marked with a letter (A, B, C, ...), not a number
structured prompt with a JSON answer schema
outputs: value v_j or 'not a scale numeral' per box letter
unit u and scale type s
indicator count and roles (hour/minute/second, decade order, or object to be measured on rulers)
M_F, the frontier's stated minors per major (soft prior only)
the frontier's own reading y_F (fallback and diagnostic only)
modules.notes: Box marks are letters because numeric marks confuse the model on number-rich images [2310.11441]; marks are placed beside, not on, each box. Unit and digit reading are the frontier's strong sub-skills [2510.26865][2604.22829]. y_F never centres a search window and never enters the margin. Input tokens, output tokens, cost and latency are logged per call and compared with a plain single-image Astra call.

modules.module: Tick-lattice extraction with local minor counting
modules.role: Measure every tick position and length, and count minors per major from the photo itself.
modules.model: Training-free: unwrap the tick band (0.6-1.0 R for dials; a band either side of the scale axis for linear scales) into a strip with 0.125 degree or 1 px columns, per-column contrast against a median face profile, 1D peak detection, 2-means clustering of tick length into major/minor. Pre-committed fallback: 30.6M U-Net tick segmenter trained on MeterFL train masks deduplicated against MeasureBench [2609.31998].
outputs: tick positions t_i, lengths l_i, major/minor flags, per-tick confidence
local minors-per-major count n_k for every major interval k and its mode M_L
modules.notes: Polar unwrapping follows MeterFL [2609.31998] without its trained segmenter in the main path. Minors are counted between each pair of measured majors, so a missed tick corrupts one interval, unlike MeterFL's count-from-start decoder. The frontier's M_F enters S(h) only through a weak prior term; when M_F and M_L disagree, the margin shrinks instead of M_F overriding the count. If the training-free extractor fails G0 on days 1-3, the MeterFL-trained segmenter becomes the extractor; the claim then becomes 'nothing is trained on any test benchmark', and MeterFL is dropped as a cross-dataset test because it would be in-distribution for the segmenter.

modules.role: Choose the scale labelling that best explains numerals, lattice and indicator together, and measure how decisive that choice is.
modules.model: Exhaustive enumeration over a small discrete space plus a hand-specified log-score with five weights; no learned parameters
inputs: tick lattice and local minor counts
outputs: winning labelling h*
value map V_h*
margin m
modules.notes: Hypotheses: for each numeral the nearest major tick and its two neighbours; per major interval an insertion or deletion of at most one minor tick; both directions; all indicator-role permutations; typically a few hundred hypotheses. The margin is computed only against rivals that change the answer by more than half a minor division, so harmless ambiguities do not cause abstention. Non-linear scales attach values to tick indices and interpolate piecewise (Reitsma excluded them [2404.08785]). The identical scorer and thresholds run on dials, clocks and linear scales; only the unwrap differs.

modules.module: Coarse pointer candidate: paste-and-compare silhouette sweep (dials and clocks)
modules.role: Pick the coarse pointer angle to within a few degrees, decide tip versus tail, reject shadows and counterweights, and separate hands.
modules.model: DINOv2 ViT-L/14 frozen, layer-18 patch descriptors as in FoundPose [2311.18809]; 2D silhouette renderer with 12 shape variants. Ablated against a pixel-space version of the same sweep (Lab colour plus gradient-orientation correlation).
inputs: rectified crop at 448 px for the feature pass
needle colour sampled near the hub
angular range: full scale arc on gauges, full circle on clocks and meter sub-dials
outputs: coarse angle phi_0 per pointer (top-3 peaks kept)
peak sharpness
modules.notes: For each candidate angle and variant the silhouette is composited onto the photo; the score is the mean cosine similarity of layer-18 descriptors between photo and composite on the patches the silhouette touches. Coarse pass at 2 degrees with 3 variants, then the top-3 peaks at 0.5 degrees with 12 variants. Because a 2-4 px needle is sub-patch at 14 px patches, the sweep is not asked for precision: its job ends at phi_0 +- 3 degrees with the tip side chosen. For clocks the sweep runs over the 720 joint (hour, minute) states, which fixes both hand angles by theta_h = 30h + m/2 [2603.08011]; an independent per-hand sweep is also run, and disagreement lowers the margin.

modules.role: Turn a coarse pointer candidate into a precise axis angle at the tick ring, independent of feature-map resolution.
modules.model: Deterministic pixel-space fit; no learned parameters
inputs: coarse angle phi_0 and tip side
outputs: refined angle phi at the tick-ring radius
axis-fit quality q (weighted residual RMS in px)
modules.notes: (1) Needle-likelihood map L(x) = 0.5 * exp(-||Lab(x) - c_n||^2 / (2 kappa^2)) + 0.5 * g_perp(x), where c_n is the median Lab colour of photo pixels under the winning silhouette at radii 0.3-0.6 R and g_perp is the normalised gradient magnitude perpendicular to the candidate ray. (2) On K = 24 circles with radii evenly spaced in [0.35 R, 0.9 R] on the tip side, sample L at 0.05 degree steps over phi_0 +- 3 degrees with bilinear interpolation; the cross-section centre phi_k is the profile maximum refined by a 3-point parabolic fit, weighted by its contrast w_k. (3) Fit a line through the points c + r_k (cos phi_k, sin phi_k) by weighted total least squares with Huber IRLS, constraining it to pass within 2 px of the pivot; circles whose residual exceeds 3 px are dropped. (4) Intersect the axis with the median radius of the measured ticks to get phi, and read it against the flanking ticks measured in the same native-resolution strip. q is the weighted residual RMS. The same refinement is applied after every coarse localiser (sweep, SAM 2 mask, radial profile, pixel sweep), so the ablation 'coarse only vs coarse + refinement' and the comparison between seeds are both clean. On linear scales the analogue is a sub-pixel change-point fit of the indicator profile along the axis.

modules.role: Locate the reading position on straight scales: liquid level or column top, or the two endpoints of a measured object on rulers.
modules.model: Training-free: 1D intensity and gradient profile along the scale axis with change-point detection for liquid columns and menisci; for rulers, Grounding DINO box of the object named by the frontier [2303.05499] prompted into SAM 2 [2408.00714], and the mask's extremes projected onto the scale axis
outputs: indicator coordinate(s) on the scale axis
profile or mask quality
modules.notes: What transfers from dials: lettered-box frontier call, lattice extraction, local minor counting, the identical labelling scorer, margin and frozen thresholds. What does not transfer: the needle silhouette sweep and pointer coupling. Vernier calipers (a main plus a vernier scale) and composite instruments are outside scope; they are detected by the frontier's scale-type answer and routed to fallback, and their share of the linear subset is reported.

modules.role: Turn the labelled lattice and indicator position into a value, decide whether to answer, and optionally return evidence to the frontier.
modules.model: Deterministic; optional second frontier call (ablation only)
outputs: reading y with unit
abstain flag
evidence JSON
modules.notes: y = V_h*(t_i) + (phi - t_i)/(t_{i+1} - t_i) * (V_h*(t_{i+1}) - V_h*(t_i)) for the flanking ticks, the local form of MeterFL's interpolation [2609.31998]; on rulers the reading is the difference of two endpoint values. Multi-dial meters use decade coupling: a higher-decade pointer's fraction within its digit must agree with the lower-decade reading. Abstain if m < tau_m or q > tau_q, thresholds fixed on the 200 MeasureBench pilot dials only; on abstention the system returns y_F flagged as unverified, so accuracy at 100% coverage is always reported.

novel_architectural_elements: The frontier model sits only on the symbolic branch (values of locally detected, letter-marked boxes, unit, scale type, indicator roles); every position, tick count and angle is measured locally, and the frontier's minors-per-major answer is a soft prior that can only shrink the margin.

Numeral values, the measured tick lattice and indicator positions meet in one jointly scored hypothesis space, and the margin to the best answer-changing rival is the system's only reliability output; it never uses the frontier's reading, confidence or self-agreement.

Pointer localisation is split into a coarse, robustness-oriented candidate stage (frozen-feature silhouette sweep, swappable with SAM 2, radial or pixel-space seeds) and a precision stage that is a fixed pixel-space axis fit, so the paper can attribute accuracy to each.
One scorer and one set of frozen thresholds serve circular dials, clocks and linear scales; only the unwrap and the indicator localiser change.
method.pseudocode:
def read_instrument(I, q, F, THR):            # THR frozen on 200 MeasureBench pilot dials
    out = []
    for D in detect_and_rectify(I):              # Grounding DINO-T + ellipse or axis fit
        boxes = dbnet(D.crop)                     # positions only
        sem = F.call(I, letter_marks(D.crop, boxes), schema=SEMANTICS)  # one API call
        strip = unwrap(D)                         # polar for dials, axis-aligned for linear
        ticks = tick_lattice(strip)               # peaks, major/minor split, local minor counts
        if D.kind in {'gauge', 'clock', 'meter_subdial'}:
            seeds = needle_sweep(D, feat=dinov2_l18, joint_clock=(D.kind == 'clock'))  # top-3, +-3 deg
            inds = [refine_tip(D.native, D.pivot, s) for s in seeds]  # pixel-space axis fit -> (phi, q)
        else:
            inds = linear_indicator(D, sem)       # change-point or SAM 2 object endpoints
        H = enumerate_labellings(boxes, sem.values, ticks, sem.scale_type, sem.roles, inds)
        S = {h: score(h, prior_M=sem.minors_per_major, w=THR.weights) for h in H}
        h_star = argmax(S)
        y = interpolate_local(h_star, ticks)
        rivals = [h for h in H if abs(value(h) - y) > 0.5 * minor_value(h_star)]
        m = S[h_star] - max(S[h] for h in rivals)
        out.append((y, m, quality(h_star)))
    y, m, qual = combine(out, sem)               # decade or hand coupling across dials
    if m < THR.tau_m or qual > THR.tau_q:
        return sem.own_reading, ABSTAIN
    return (y, sem.unit), ANSWER
design_choices: Credit and delta: the semantics-to-VLM, geometry-to-deterministic-pipeline split is the design recommendation of [2604.22829]; this paper's contribution is the first measured single-image instantiation on public real-image benchmarks, plus the labelling margin, the better-views control and frozen-threshold transfer, not the split itself.

The frontier reads values but not positions or counts: its unit and digit reading are strong [2510.26865][2604.22829] while fine spatial grounding and minor-tick counting are its named failures [2510.26865]; this also removes Reitsma's dominant OCR-recognition failure [2404.08785].

Letter marks, placed beside boxes: Set-of-Mark reports that numeric marks confuse GPT-4V on number-rich images and that centred marks can be misattributed [2310.11441]; the frontier's box-value accuracy is reported as a function of box density so this choice is checked.

Joint ranking of neighbouring labellings rather than sequential rounding (numeral -> major -> minor): an early wrong attachment cannot silently propagate, and the score gap to answer-changing rivals gives abstention for free; this is ordinary MAP-with-margin and is claimed only as a measured mechanism, with the sequential version as an ablation.
Local minor counting between measured majors rather than counting from the scale start as in MeterFL [2609.31998]: a missed tick then corrupts one interval rather than every later index.

Coarse-then-refine pointer localisation: FoundPose itself needs featuremetric refinement because 14 px patches limit precision [2311.18809]; here the precision stage is a pixel-space axis fit so that it cannot depend on patch size, and the frozen-feature sweep must earn its place against SAM 2 [2408.00714], radial-profile and pixel-space seeds.
Full-range candidate search rather than a window around the frontier reading: frontier readings can be a whole interval off or collapse to 10:10 [2510.26865].
Abstention independent of the frontier: VLM-derived confidence fails where perception fails [2610.04836][2512.06373][2608.17723].
Thresholds are set once and frozen: every cross-dataset and linear-scale number uses the 200-pilot-dial thresholds, so 'training-free generalises' is tested rather than asserted.
method.theoretical_grounding: Two simple conditions explain when the method should work and are measured rather than assumed. (1) Numeral attachment: the nearest-major assignment of numeral j is correct if |u_j - t_pi(j)| < Delta_major / 2, where Delta_major is the major-tick spacing; with 2, 5 or 10 minors per major this tolerance is about 13-27 degrees on common gauges. With n >= 2 numerals and a monotone, arithmetic (or monotone for non-linear) value constraint, a wrong labelling needs several numerals displaced in the same direction, which the joint score penalises. The 150 annotated held-out dials give the empirical distribution of |u_j - t_pi(j)| / Delta_major. (2) Reading precision: with local interpolation, reading error in minor divisions equals the angular error of phi plus tick-position error divided by the local minor spacing; for a 270-degree scale with 50 minors (5.4 degrees each), a 0.5-degree pointer error is under 0.1 division, well inside MeasureBench's per-image intervals [2510.26865]. The tip refinement fits a line to K = 24 cross-section centres; with sub-pixel centroid error sigma_p and needle length L px, the axis-angle error scales as about sigma_p / (L sqrt(K/12)), i.e. well under 0.5 degree for L >= 80 px and sigma_p <= 1 px, independent of the 14 px patch size. The margin is a log-score difference between the best and the best answer-changing labelling; thresholding it is standard selective prediction. These are design arguments, not proofs; the day-1-3 pilot measures whether they hold on web photos.

model_details.base_model: No model is trained or fine-tuned in the main method. Frozen components: GPT-6 Astra (black-box API, default effort, one call per image); DINOv2 ViT-L/14 layer-18 patch descriptors [2311.18809]; SAM 2 (image mode, point/box prompts) for the hub-prompted needle baseline and ruler object masks [2408.00714]; DBNet ResNet-18 with public scene-text weights [1911.08947]; Grounding DINO-T [2303.05499]. Local coarse-code variant: Qwen3-VL-4B in place of Astra. Pre-committed fallback: 30.6M U-Net tick/pointer segmenter as in MeterFL [2609.31998].

training.method: No model training for the main method (training-free inference with a hand-specified score whose five weights and two thresholds are set once on 200 MeasureBench pilot dials). Fallback only: supervised segmentation of tick and pointer masks on MeterFL train masks deduplicated against MeasureBench, never on any test image. Clock baseline only: if the It's About Time checkpoint is not downloadable, retrain its public code on its synthetic generator, reported as such [2111.09162].
objective_functions: Purpose: pick the scale labelling that best explains numerals, ticks and indicators. Formally: S(h) = sum_j log N(u_j - t_pi(j); 0, sigma_n^2) + lambda_1 sum_k log p(n_k | M_L, delta) + lambda_M log p(M_L | M_F) + lambda_2 log p(V_h | s) + lambda_3 log p(phi | rho, coupling), where n_k is the corrected minor count in major interval k, M_L the locally counted mode, M_F the frontier's stated value (weak prior, lambda_M small and fixed), p(V_h | s) rewards arithmetic (linear) or monotone (non-linear) value progressions, and the coupling term enforces theta_h = 30h + m/2 on clocks or decade consistency on meters.

Purpose: find coarse pointer candidates robust to shadows and counterweights. Formally: phi_0 = argmax_{phi, s} (1/|P(phi,s)|) sum_{p in P(phi,s)} cos(f_18(I)_p, f_18(I composited with silhouette(phi, s))_p), with P(phi,s) the patches the silhouette touches and f_18 frozen DINOv2 layer-18 descriptors.

Purpose: refine the pointer axis at native resolution. Formally: minimise sum_k w_k rho_Huber(dist(p_k, line(c', phi))) subject to ||c' - c|| <= 2 px, with p_k the parabolic-refined cross-section centres on K = 24 circles.

Purpose: decide when to answer. Formally: answer iff m = S(h*) - max_{h: |V_h(phi) - V_h*(phi)| > 0.5 minor} S(h) >= tau_m and q <= tau_q, with tau_m, tau_q chosen on the 200 pilot dials to maximise value+unit accuracy at 100% coverage with fallback, then frozen.
Purpose (fallback segmenter only): learn tick and pointer masks. Formally: L = L_CE(mask_pred, mask_gt) + L_Dice(mask_pred, mask_gt) on MeterFL training masks.
training.adaptation: None for the main method; fallback segmenter trained from scratch (30.6M parameters) in a few GPU-hours on one RTX 4090.

key_hyperparameters.polar_strip: 2880 angular bins (0.125 degree) x 128 radial bins over 0.6-1.0 R, at native resolution
key_hyperparameters.needle_sweep: coarse 2 deg with 3 variants; top-3 peaks at 0.5 deg with 12 variants; output phi_0 +- 3 deg
key_hyperparameters.tip_refinement: K = 24 circles in [0.35 R, 0.9 R]; 0.05 deg sampling; Huber IRLS; pivot tolerance 2 px; circle rejection at 3 px residual
key_hyperparameters.dinov2_input: 448 px rectified crop, layer 18 of ViT-L/14
key_hyperparameters.labelling_neighbourhood: numeral-to-major offset in {-1,0,+1}; at most one minor insertion or deletion per major interval; both directions; all indicator-role permutations
key_hyperparameters.sigma_n: one quarter of the measured major-tick spacing
key_hyperparameters.frozen_on_pilot: lambda_1, lambda_2, lambda_3, lambda_M, tau_m, tau_q (sigma_n fixed by rule)
key_hyperparameters.fallback_segmenter: U-Net 30.6M, Adam lr 1e-3, 100 epochs on deduplicated MeterFL train masks

related_methods: GPT-6 Astra alone: default, high and xhigh reasoning effort, with and without its built-in Python/crop tools [2609.35718].
GPT-6 Astra with better views: the method's rectified crop, unwrapped strip and lettered tick and numeral marks as a visual prompt, without the computed answer (Set-of-Mark style [2310.11441]).
Lost in Motion design guidance: VLM for semantics, edge/Hough geometry for the needle, rule-based validation [2604.22829].
Gemini-2.5-Pro on MeasureBench: 31.5% real dials, 21.9% real linear (2025 figures) [2510.26865].
TriSCA: trained Qwen3-VL-4B, 28.5% on MeasureBench real dials [2604.26614].
Reitsma et al.: modular trained gauge reader with OCR numeral anchoring, 8.5% on MeasureBench real images [2404.08785][2510.26865].
MeterFL pipeline: trained U-Net tick segmentation, polar unwrap and metadata-supplied counting, 87.2% Acc on its own test set [2609.31998].
DialBench MRLM: end-to-end trained pointer-meter VLM on RPM-10K [2511.21982].
It's About Time: trained 720-state clock reader, 18.54% full-time on TickTockVQA [2111.09162][2603.08011].
Swap-DPO on TickTockVQA: LoRA SFT + DPO clock reader [2603.08011].
key_differences: vs. Lost in Motion [2604.22829]: that paper states the split as guidance from a three-instrument video study and proposes Hough geometry; this paper builds it for single images, replaces line fits with a ranked labelling plus a pixel-space axis fit, adds a frontier-independent margin, and measures it on five public real-image sets with frozen thresholds.

vs. Astra with more effort, tools or better views: the frontier never reads a position; one default-effort call supplies only semantics, and the better-views baseline tests whether showing Astra the same measured views would be enough.

vs. TriSCA, DialBench, It's About Time and Swap-DPO: no weights are changed and nothing is trained on instrument data, so the method applies to an API-only model; cross-dataset transfer with frozen thresholds is measured, not asserted.

vs. Reitsma: the frontier replaces OCR recognition, readings come from measured minor ticks rather than linear interpolation between numerals, non-linear scales need no global model, and a coarse-seed-plus-axis-fit replaces the segmented line fit and 'closer end' heuristic.

vs. MeterFL: v_min, delta_v and tick values are read by the frontier rather than supplied, minors are counted locally, and alternative labellings are ranked with a margin instead of one deterministic count from the scale start.
vs. RSure-style or rethink-turn arbitration: the reliability signal (labelling margin and axis-fit quality) never uses the frontier's own visual reading.

proposed_evaluation.evaluation_setting: Single-image instrument reading with GPT-6 Astra as the black-box system being helped, inside the Constraints: all experiments finish by 2026-11-09, API spend at most US$1,000 with per-call cost measured, local compute <= 40 GPU-days on 24 GB GPUs (estimated about 20: about 30 s of ViT-L passes per dial image and 55 s per clock for the sweep over about 8,700 local runs, x3 for ablations, plus SAM 2, Qwen3-VL-4B and a possible 2-3 GPU-day clock-baseline retrain). DATA AVAILABILITY (checked 2026-10-18): MeasureBench and TickTockVQA are public; MeterFL is public on GitHub with train/test split and readings [2609.31998]; RPM-10K is downloadable with an 8,730/2,000 instance-disjoint split and released MRLM weights [2511.21982]; InSituMeasure has no public release (no URL in the paper, none found by search) [2609.04014], so it is used only if released before 2026-11-02, on its analog-pointer categories with the same frozen thresholds. SPLITS: MeasureBench dials 200 pilot (the only tuning data) / 511 test, all 511 tagged by family and nuisance before any run, 150 of them additionally annotated with major-tick positions, numeral-to-tick assignment and pointer angles by annotators who never see predictions; MeasureBench linear 80 development (indicator-module debugging only, no weight or threshold change) / 281 test; TickTockVQA 150 train-split clocks (debugging and G3 gate only, not thresholds) / a seeded random 1,000-image test list released with the paper, plus the full 5,247-image test set for local-only components and It's About Time; MeterFL 269 reading test images minus any dHash near-duplicate of a MeasureBench image (MeterFL lists MeasureBench as an image source); RPM-10K a released stratified 400-image sample of the 2,000 held-out images for API runs, all 2,000 for the fully local variant and MRLM. FREEZE: on 2026-10-28 the thresholds, code hash and all image lists are committed to a timestamped public repository; nothing is changed afterwards. SCHEDULE: day 1-3 (10-19 to 10-21) G0 component pilot and strongest-Astra measurement on 50 tagged pilot dials, before the needle sweep is built, with availability checks for every checkpoint and dataset; 10-22 to 10-27 needle sweep, refinement, needle baselines, clock and linear modules, full 200-pilot run and gates G1-G3; annotation of the 150 held-out dials runs in parallel from day 1; 10-28 freeze; 10-28 to 11-05 test runs; 11-06 to 11-09 buffer. G0 GO/NO-GO (10-21, 50 pilot dials): (a) lattice resolvable on >= 60% and numeral-to-major assignment correct on >= 80% of dials with >= 2 detected numerals; (b) frontier semantics + ground-truth lattice and pointer (oracle geometry) reads >= 80% correctly; (c) Astra-best on the 50 dials <= 50% value+unit. If (a) fails with the training-free extractor but passes with the MeterFL-trained segmenter, switch to it (MeterFL then leaves the cross-dataset set). If (b) fails, the semantic channel is the bottleneck and the run stops. If (c) fails, +15 over Astra-best is infeasible at the committed selective operating point and the run stops; the outcome is a measurement paper (Astra configurations and oracle splits). BUDGET RULE: on days 1-3 measure mean cost per default call c_0 and per xhigh+tools call c_x. Tier 1 (always): Astra-default plain, the method's semantic call and the better-views call on all 2,891 API images (711 + 361 + 1,150 + 269 + 400). Tier 2: xhigh+tools plain on 200 pilot + 511 test dials, 300 of the 1,000 clocks and 150 each of linear, MeterFL and RPM-10K; better-views xhigh+tools on the 711 dials; high effort on the 200 pilot dials (to select Astra-best). Tier 3: a second sample of Astra-default and Astra-best on 200 test dials for variance. If projected Tier 1 + Tier 2 exceeds US$800, Tier 2 subsets outside the 711 dials are cut first, never below 511 test dials; US$200 is held in reserve. ASTRA-BEST is selected on the pilot among {default, high, xhigh+tools, better-views default, better-views xhigh+tools} and fixed for test; all configurations run on a set are reported. SIZING: with a paired design and about 30% discordant items, the paired SE is about 3.9 points at n = 200 and about 2.4 at n = 511, so +15 is resolvable on the test set, and nuisance and family claims are made only on subsets of at least 100 test images.

main_metrics: Value and value+unit accuracy at 100% coverage (fallback on abstention), with paired-bootstrap 95% CIs
Gain decomposition against Astra-best and against Astra-default: coverage, the method's selective accuracy, Astra's accuracy on the same covered items, and Astra's accuracy on the abstained items
Selective accuracy and coverage at the frozen thresholds; area under the risk-coverage curve

Error detection AUROC on one error definition (the method's pre-fallback reading is wrong) for every signal: labelling margin, axis-fit quality, Astra verbalised confidence and Astra 3-sample agreement; separately, each Astra signal for Astra's own errors; also on items where Astra's samples agree but are wrong
Per-family accuracy, coverage and gain: single-pointer gauges, clocks, multi-dial meters, linear vs non-linear dial scales, linear instruments by type, TickTockVQA clock types

Component metrics on the 150 annotated test dials: DBNet numeral recall, numeral-to-major assignment accuracy, tick recall/precision, local minors-per-major accuracy vs Astra's M_F accuracy, Astra box-value accuracy vs box density (boxes per 90 degrees), pointer angle error in degrees by seed and with or without refinement, peak sharpness by nuisance tag
Oracle splits on the 150 annotated dials: ground-truth pointer (scale-only) and ground-truth labelling (pointer-only)
TickTockVQA exact-minute accuracy, hour and minute accuracy, Tol-1 and Tol-5, MAE in minutes, hour/minute swap rate
MeterFL Acc and median %FS; RPM-10K Accuracy-epsilon and within-half-minor accuracy

Measured API cost per image, input and output tokens of the semantic call vs a plain Astra call, frontier calls per image, end-to-end latency including local GPU-seconds; Astra run-to-run SD from Tier 3
ablations: Joint labelling ranking vs sequential rounding (numeral -> major -> minor) on the same lattice
Local minor counting vs MeterFL-style counting from the scale start; frontier M_F as soft prior vs hard constraint vs removed
Letter marks vs numeric marks on the numeral boxes; DBNet positions vs positions estimated by the frontier
Pointer seed: DINOv2 sweep vs pixel-space sweep vs SAM 2 hub mask vs radial profile vs Hough, each with and without the tip refinement
Candidate range: full arc or circle vs +-1 major interval around y_F vs +-1 minor around y_F
Clock-hand coupling (joint 720-state sweep) and decade coupling on/off
Abstention signal: margin vs axis-fit quality vs both vs Astra self-agreement
Tick extraction: training-free peaks vs the MeterFL-trained U-Net (reported on non-MeterFL sets)
Evidence use: answer returned directly vs a second frontier call composing the answer from the evidence (how often Astra overrides correct evidence)
Semantic reader: GPT-6 Astra vs Qwen3-VL-4B

falsifiable_predictions.pillar: Day-1-3 component pilot and strongest-Astra measurement (G0, go/no-go)
falsifiable_predictions.prediction: Predicted, not observed: on 50 tagged pilot dials the training-free lattice is resolvable on >= 60%, numeral-to-major assignment is correct on >= 80% of dials with >= 2 detected numerals, oracle-geometry reading with frontier semantics is >= 80%, and Astra-best reads <= 50% value+unit.
falsifiable_predictions.kill_condition: Assignment < 70% with both the training-free and the MeterFL-trained extractor, or oracle-geometry reading < 70%, or Astra-best > 55%: the run stops on 2026-10-21 and the method paper is not written.

falsifiable_predictions.pillar: Headline accuracy, absolute floor and gain decomposition (G1)
falsifiable_predictions.prediction: Predicted: on the 511 held-out MeasureBench dials, value+unit accuracy at 100% coverage is >= 50% absolute and >= Astra-best + 15 points (paired-bootstrap 95% lower bound > 0) at <= 1.3x Astra-default measured API cost per image; in the decomposition, coverage >= 50%, selective accuracy >= 75%, Astra-best accuracy on the covered items <= 55%, and the fallback term costs at most 3 points.
falsifiable_predictions.kill_condition: Gain < 10 points or lower bound <= 0 on the pilot (gate) or test; or absolute accuracy < 45%; or Astra-best accuracy on covered items >= 60% (the method only answers dials Astra already reads); or Astra xhigh+tools within 5 points at <= 2x the method's cost.

falsifiable_predictions.prediction: Predicted: with every weight and threshold frozen from the MeasureBench pilot, the method beats Astra-default by >= 10 points on MeterFL test (Acc within two minor divisions, MeasureBench near-duplicates removed) and by >= 10 points on the 400 RPM-10K held-out images (within half a minor division), reaching >= 65% MeterFL Acc, with margin AUROC >= 0.75 on each set.
falsifiable_predictions.kill_condition: Gain < 5 points on either set, or margin AUROC < 0.65 on either: the claim that training-free reading transfers across datasets is withdrawn and reported as negative.

falsifiable_predictions.prediction: Predicted: on the 511 test dials the method beats the best better-views Astra configuration by >= 10 points, and better views recover at most one third of the method's gain over plain Astra-default.
falsifiable_predictions.kill_condition: Better-views Astra within 5 points of the method: the contribution is reframed as visual prompting and the local-measurement claim is dropped.

falsifiable_predictions.pillar: Pointer localisation: frozen-feature sweep and tip refinement (G2)
falsifiable_predictions.prediction: Predicted: with the same refinement for every seed, the DINOv2 sweep beats the best of SAM 2 hub mask, radial profile and pixel-space sweep by >= 5 points overall and >= 10 points on the pooled shadow/glare, counterweight, tapered or hollow and multi-hand test dials (n >= 100); refinement cuts median pointer error by >= 50% for every seed.
falsifiable_predictions.kill_condition: Gain over the best alternative seed < 2 points overall or < 5 on the pooled nuisance subset: the best alternative becomes the reported seed; if the pixel-space sweep matches DINOv2 within 2 points, the claim is restated as the silhouette sweep, not the frozen features.

limitations: The semantics/geometry split is anticipated by [2604.22829] and each module has a close ancestor (MeterFL unwrap and interpolation, Reitsma numeral anchoring, FoundPose render-and-compare, the 720-state clock space of It's About Time); the contribution is the measured instantiation, the frontier-independent margin and the transfer tests, and the paper stands or falls on its numbers.

Training-free geometry is exactly where earlier pipelines collapsed in the wild (Reitsma 8.5% on MeasureBench, Sobel+Hough clocks below 10%) [2510.26865][2111.09162]; coverage, not accuracy, may cap the gain, which is why the day-1-3 pilot is a go/no-go and the MeterFL-trained segmenter is the pre-committed fallback.

Scope is instruments with a visible tick lattice: dials, clocks and single-scale linear instruments; vernier calipers, composite and digital instruments are routed to the frontier, and illustrated or tick-free clocks will mostly abstain.

The method depends on the frontier for numeral values, units, scale type and indicator roles; misreads of decimals, overlaid scales or unusual units propagate, and only one frontier model (plus a local Qwen3-VL-4B variant) is tested.

Some evidence rests on data that may not be available in time: InSituMeasure is not public as of 2026-10-18 [2609.04014], It's About Time weights may need retraining [2111.09162], and MeterFL shares image sources with MeasureBench [2609.31998]; MeasureBench may also be in Astra's training data, which biases comparisons against the method.
